title.title: A counterexample to Pixton's completeness conjecture
title.subtitle: Claim: a tautological class outside the span of Pixton's relations vanishes in Chow and in cohomology

plain: A proposed complete rulebook for curve-counting classes misses a rule, found at a vast genus

lines.note: the moduli space of stable curves

beats.text: Pixton's relations hold among tautological classes; are they all of them?
The claimed counterexample lives in genus $10^{60}$
No computer can check an example this large; it rests on the proof

steps: Take corrected small diagonals on powers of the universal curve
Multiply them with alternating signs: the class vanishes
Yet it is not built from Pixton's relations

achievement.label: Pixton's completeness conjecture (2012)
achievement.context: Before: the relations were proved valid (Pandharipande–Pixton–Zvonkine 2015; Janda 2017)
achievement.note: Only Pixton's original system; extended relation systems may survive

verify.detail: No Lean; the 61-page proof is the only check
verify.ourCheck: We read the claim and caveats; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Pixton listed relations among tautological classes and conjectured they are all of them.
An alternating product of small diagonals vanishes, but is not in Pixton's span.
Claimed: a missing relation, in Chow and cohomology.

sources.quote: the example has genus 10^60 and 3·C(10^60,3) markings

Pixton (2012) proposed the graph-formula relations and conjectured they generate all tautological relations; validity proved in cohomology by Pandharipande–Pixton–Zvonkine (JAMS 2015) and in Chow by Janda (2017)
